summary.headline: H1 FY27 revenue rose 33% YoY to Rs 1,639 crore, but PAT fell to Rs 55.6 crore as lead margins compressed on supply disruption and input costs.
summary.overview: Pondy Oxides reported H1 FY27 revenue of Rs 1,639 crore (up 33% YoY), driven by copper, which grew about 4.5x and contributed about 47% of the top line. H1 PAT was Rs 55.6 crore, and operating cash flow turned positive while the company stayed net cash and debt-free. Lead volumes and value-added mix were hit by West Asia-linked shipping and raw material disruption, and lead EBITDA per tonne fell to about Rs 16,000 in Q2 from about Rs 21,000 in Q1. Management guided that the turnaround comes in Q4 FY27 as contracts are renegotiated and sourcing is realigned, and it cut the FY27 lead volume target.

financial_highlights.metric: Lead value-added share of volume (Q2 FY27)

financial_highlights.value: Net cash and debt-free; operating cash flow positive in H1

segments.name: Lead
segments.commentary: Volumes and value-added mix were hit by supply disruption; value-added share fell to 60-65% in Q2 from about 85% in Q1, and EBITDA was about Rs 2.5/kg below the guided Rs 18-20/kg band. Management now expects about 25,000 t per quarter from next year, and FY27 lead volume guidance of 1.2-1.3 lakh t is withdrawn; FY27 sales of about 95,000 t is 'closer to' target.

segments.name: Copper
segments.commentary: Copper revenue grew about 4.5x in H1 to 47% of the top line, with EBITDA of Rs 44,536/t (+30% YoY). Recycling capacity of 12,000 t/yr (6,000 t added in Q4 FY26) is targeted at about 90% utilisation in FY27; FY27 copper sales of about 10,000 t is guided, with over 20,000 t targeted next year.

guidance_outlook: Lead volume: about 25,000 t per quarter (about 1 lakh t/yr) targeted for next financial year on a status-quo assumption of continued disruption; FY27 lead volume target of 1.2-1.3 lakh t withdrawn.
Lead EBITDA back to Rs 18,000-20,000/t guidance as volumes improve; turnaround expected from Q4 FY27, with Q3 still under pressure.
Copper EBITDA guidance: Rs 35,000-40,000/t on recycling and about Rs 65,000/t on cathode, reiterated.
Copper cathode phase 1 (18,000 t/yr) commissioning by Dec 2026 with trial runs in Q4 FY27; phase 2 (balance 18,000 t/yr) by Q3 FY28.
Long-term 2030 roadmap reiterated: over 15% volume growth, 20%+ revenue and profit CAGR, EBITDA margin over 8%, ROCE above 20%, over 60% revenue from value-added products.
Copper share of revenue expected at about 45% in FY27.
capex_capacity: Copper cathode facility of 36,000 t/yr at Tamil Nadu (Terawai Kandikei) with investment of about Rs 200 crore, funded by internal accruals; about Rs 60 crore spent so far.
Stage 1 spend of about Rs 140 crore expected to complete in the next 2-3 months; the balance about Rs 60 crore falls in phase 2 next financial year. Installation starts early December.
Expanded lead capacity of 72,000 t/yr operated at about 40% utilisation in FY27, expected to reach about 70% in coming quarters as supply conditions improve.
Copper recycling capacity of 12,000 t/yr after 6,000 t incremental added in Q4 FY26; targeted about 90% utilisation in FY27.
demand_pricing: Lead realisation averaged about Rs 260/kg; mix shift toward tin alloys (tin about USD 45,000/t) lifts realisation but not necessarily EBITDA per tonne.

Cost pass-through: first-round quotations to battery customers submitted, with second-round talks due for Jan-Feb contract start; management says buyer resistance is lower because they also face raw material shortages.
Value-added lead margin premium over pure lead is about 0.75-1.25 percentage points on average.
Management sees structural copper supply-demand gap in India; about 80% of cathode feed to remain imported, with domestic sourcing rising to about 20% over the next year or two.
Domestic lead/scrap procurement is slightly more expensive than international sourcing.
Lead procurement shifted toward South America, Southeast Asia and domestic; Middle East sourcing (about 5-8%) dropped.

qa_highlights.question: Why did lead EBITDA per kg and value-added mix fall sharply in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Value-added mix fell to 60-65% from about 85% in Q1 because customers took more pure lead; higher power, fuel, flux, logistics and shipping costs cut EBITDA by about Rs 2.5/kg. Management says the pressure was highest in Q2 and turnaround starts in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Will lead volume guidance of 1.2-1.3 lakh t for FY27 be met?
qa_highlights.answer: No; management said the FY27 guidance does not hold given the drastic erosion from supply chain disruption. FY27 sales could be closer to 95,000 t, with about 1 lakh t targeted next year.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a lower copper EBITDA per tonne trend and will guidance change?
qa_highlights.answer: The Q1 copper spike to about Rs 48,000/t was a one-off from market squeeze and demand; guidance of Rs 35,000-40,000/t on recycling and about Rs 65,000/t on cathode is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company set up overseas raw material warehouses?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management prefers exclusive tie-ups with larger yards rather than overseas collection points, citing holding cost, shipping risk and fragmented metal flows.

qa_highlights.question: Will the cathode project face hedging or LME registration constraints?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said hedging and LME registration are separate; all recycled and cathode copper is hedged, and LME registration gives deliverability and quality reassurance but does not guarantee sales.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the copper EBITDA rise in Q1 and is the pricing outlook sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described the Q1 elevated copper margin as a one-off from a market squeeze and demand-led higher realisations; the recycling guidance is still Rs 35,000-40,000/t.

risks_watch: Shipping and raw material availability for lead; progress of Q4 turnaround and FY28 target of about 25,000 t per quarter.
Pass-through of higher freight, fuel and flux costs in Jan-Feb contract renewals with battery customers.
Cathode phase 1 commissioning by Dec 2026, phase 2 by Q3 FY28, and dependence on about 80% imported copper scrap.
Lead value-added mix recovery from 60-65% toward the 60%+ long-term target; shift by customers toward pure lead.
Analyst questions on peer comparison and gross margin; management disputed the view that the company is underperforming peers.
Possible EU scrap export restrictions (currently mainly aluminium-related; copper from Europe about 5-8% of imports).
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term copper growth and the cathode build-out, but defensive on lead: management withdrew the FY27 lead volume target, attributed margin pressure to supply disruption and costs, and deflected several questions on competitors and related-party share sales.

adds.what: Copper cathode facility 36,000 t/yr at Terawai Kandikei, Tamil Nadu (phase 1 18,000 t/yr)

growth.why: Management cut the FY27 lead volume guidance (1.2-1.3 lakh t withdrawn, FY27 near 95,000 t) and sees the lead turnaround only from Q4 FY27, but reiterated copper EBITDA guidance and a copper cathode plant (18,000 t phase 1 commissioning Dec 2026, phase 2 by Q3 FY28) backed by Rs 200 crore internal accruals, with lead capacity at only 40% utilisation.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Lead EBITDA fell to about Rs 16,000/t in Q2 from about Rs 21,000/t in Q1 and management guides back to Rs 18,000-20,000/t as the turnaround starts in Q4 FY27, while copper recycling EBITDA is held at Rs 35,000-40,000/t.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Copper cathode phase 1 of 18,000 t/yr is targeted for commissioning by December 2026 with installation starting early December, and phase 2 of the balance 18,000 t/yr by Q3 FY28; Rs 140 crore of the Rs 200 crore stage-1 spend is due in 2-3 months.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 lead guidance of 1.2-1.3 lakh t is withdrawn (FY27 near 95,000 t), but lead is targeted at about 25,000 t/quarter next year and copper sales are about 10,000 t in FY27 with over 20,000 t next year.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Lead capacity of 72,000 t/yr runs at about 40% utilisation, so no new lead capex is needed, and the copper cathode build-out of Rs 200 crore is already committed; a further copper capex announcement depends on recycling reaching about 90% utilisation from 12,000 t/yr.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Lead FY27 volume guidance was cut and withdrawn, and the lead turnaround only starts in Q4 FY27, with Q3 still under pressure.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Lead volumes are at about 40% utilisation of 72,000 t/yr, the FY27 volume target has already been cut, and Jan-Feb battery contract renewals depend on pass-through of higher freight, fuel and flux costs.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: The copper cathode plant (phase 1 of 18,000 t/yr, trial runs in Q4 FY27) is the new product line, and management is shifting lead mix toward tin alloys, though the tin-alloy shift lifts realisation but not EBITDA per tonne.

rows.label: Lead cost pass-through in Jan-Feb contracts
rows.why: First-round quotes are submitted and second-round talks are due for a Jan-Feb start, and management says buyer resistance is lower because customers also face raw material shortages; the Rs 2.5/kg EBITDA hit is the amount to recover.

rows.label: Lead EBITDA recovery to Rs 18,000-20,000/t
rows.why: Lead EBITDA was about Rs 16,000/t in Q2 versus Rs 21,000/t in Q1, and management expects the turnaround from Q4 FY27 as volumes improve, with Q3 still under pressure.

rows.label: Lead utilisation rising from 40% to about 70%
rows.why: The 72,000 t/yr lead capacity is at about 40% utilisation in FY27 and management expects about 70% as supply conditions improve, which depends on the shipping and raw material disruption easing.

tone.note: Management was confident on copper growth, the Rs 200 crore cathode build-out and reiterated copper EBITDA guidance, but defensive on lead after withdrawing the FY27 volume target; analysts pushed on lead margins, peer comparison, gross margin and related-party share sales.
